data.title: Telecom Subscription Velocity — Multiple New Service Activations From Same Identity/Device Within 30 Days
data.description: Detects subscription fraud patterns where the same identity or device IMEI is used to activate multiple new telecom service accounts within a 30-day window. Subscription fraud is the top concern for 53% of telecom executives (TransUnion 2025). Fraudsters use synthetic identities (TP-0003) with GenAI-generated KYC documents to open accounts across multiple carriers, acquiring subsidized flagship devices on installment plans with no payment intent. The multi-carrier activation pattern is the strongest detection signal, as legitimate customers rarely activate 3+ accounts across 2+ carriers in a 30-day period. Devices acquired through subscription fraud are resold at 60-80% of retail value on secondary markets.

enrichment_required.source: Rolling 30-day count of new account activations per identity hash
Distinct carrier count per identity hash in 30-day window
Credit bureau data on identity's credit history length

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Telecom Subscription Velocity — DL-0184")`
`comment("Detects multiple new service activations from same identity/device within 30 days")`
index=flame_telecom sourcetype=flame:account_activations
  activation_type="new_account"
| bin _time span=30d
| stats count as activation_count,
        dc(carrier_id) as unique_carriers,
        dc(device_imei) as unique_devices,
        values(carrier_id) as carriers,
        values(device_imei) as devices,
        values(device_model) as device_models,
        values(plan_type) as plan_types,
        sum(device_value) as total_device_value,
        earliest(_time) as first_activation,
        latest(_time) as last_activation
  by identity_hash, _time
| where activation_count >= 3 OR unique_carriers >= 2
| eval risk_score = case(
    activation_count >= 5 AND unique_carriers >= 3, "critical",
    activation_count >= 4 AND total_device_value > 5000, "high",
    activation_count >= 3 OR unique_carriers >= 2, "medium")
| eval days_between = round((last_activation - first_activation) / 86400, 1)
| table identity_hash, activation_count, unique_carriers, unique_devices,
        carriers, devices, device_models, plan_types, total_device_value,
        first_activation, last_activation, days_between, risk_score
| sort - activation_count
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Telecom Subscription Velocity
-- Detects multiple new service activations from same identity/device within 30 days
SELECT
  a.identity_hash,
  COUNT(*) AS activation_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT a.carrier_id) AS unique_carriers,
  COUNT(DISTINCT a.device_imei) AS unique_devices,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT a.carrier_id, ', ') AS carriers,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT a.device_model, ', ') AS device_models,
  SUM(a.device_value) AS total_device_value,
  AVG(a.device_value) AS avg_device_value,
  MIN(a.activation_date) AS first_activation,
  MAX(a.activation_date) AS last_activation,
  DATEDIFF(DAY, MIN(a.activation_date), MAX(a.activation_date)) AS window_days,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(*) >= 5 AND COUNT(DISTINCT a.carrier_id) >= 3 THEN 'critical'
    WHEN COUNT(*) >= 4 AND SUM(a.device_value) > 5000 THEN 'high'
    ELSE 'medium'
  END AS risk_score
FROM account_activations a
WHERE a.activation_type = 'new_account'
  AND a.activation_date >= DATEADD(DAY, -30, CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY a.identity_hash
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 OR COUNT(DISTINCT a.carrier_id) >= 2
ORDER BY activation_count DESC
queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL for Telecom Subscription Velocity
activation_type="new_account"
| groupBy(identity_hash, function=[
    count(as=activation_count),
    countDistinct(carrier_id, as=unique_carriers),
    countDistinct(device_imei, as=unique_devices),
    sum(device_value, as=total_device_value),
    collect([carrier_id, device_model, device_imei, plan_type]),
    min(activation_date, as=first_activation),
    max(activation_date, as=last_activation)
  ], span=30d)
| activation_count >= 3 OR unique_carriers >= 2
| sort(activation_count, order=desc)

references: Subex, Global Telecom Fraud Intelligence Report (2025, 2026)
falsepositives: Corporate accounts activating multiple lines for new employees
Legitimate device upgrades across carrier switches during promotional periods
Family plan activations where multiple members onboard simultaneously
Resellers and authorized dealers activating demonstration or inventory devices
